response.description: Response specification keyed by status code.

side_effects.description: Side effects of this API call.

Architecture.description:
The Architecture describes the high-level structure of the software —
layers, modules, components, and communication patterns.

communication.description: Communication patterns between parts of the system.

depends_on.description: Other modules this module depends on.

responsibility.description: What this module is responsible for.

Behavior.description:
The Behavior section describes the dynamic aspects of the software:
function signatures with pseudocode logic, complex multi-participant
flows, and state machines.

description.description: Description of what this concept represents.

invariants.description: Invariants that must always hold true.

action.description: The action to take when the condition is met.

condition.description: The condition that triggers this rule.

dependencies.description: Other contracts this class depends on.

preconditions.description: Conditions that must be true before calling.

Contracts.description:
The Contracts section defines the interfaces, classes, enums,
and API endpoints that form the software's public contract.

This is the "contract-first" core: everything is described by its
input/output signatures, behavior, pre/post conditions, and error cases.

identity.description: Whether this is the identity / primary key.

internal.description: Whether this is internal (not exposed to clients).

DataModel.description:
A Data Model describes a data entity — its logical meaning,
physical representation, attributes, relationships, and validation rules.

description.description: What this entity represents in the domain.

logical_model.description: The logical model — business meaning in natural language.

validation_rules.description: Validation rules that apply to this entity.

type.description: Type of dependency (e.g., runtime, build, dev).

DesignDecision.description:
A record of a design decision, its context, alternatives considered,
rationale, and consequences.

Every significant architectural or design choice should be captured here.

constraints.description: Additional constraints imposed by this decision.

context.description: The context in which the decision was made.

topic.description: The topic / area this decision applies to.

Domain.description:
The Domain Layer describes the business problem domain — the concepts,
rules, and processes that the software models and automates.

This is the anchor for all other layers: code and data structures exist
to operate on these business concepts.

business_concepts.description: Business concepts — the nouns of the domain.

secret.description: Indicates this value is a secret.

scenario.description: The scenario that triggers the exception.

compensation.description: Compensation strategy if rollback is needed.

edge_cases.description: Edge cases and their expected behavior.

logic.description: Pseudocode logic (using S.DEF standard pseudocode syntax).

pure_function.description: Whether this function is pure (no side effects).

invariants.description: Invariants that all implementations must maintain.

is_abstract.description: Indicates this is abstract and must be implemented.

entry_condition.description: Condition that triggers entry into this stage.

exit_condition.description: Condition that must be met to exit this stage.

priority.description: Priority level: must, should, or may.

ReconstructionRules.description:
Reconstruction Rules guide the builder agent in how to reconstruct
the software from the S.DEF description.

This includes the target fidelity level, technology stack constraints,
and priority-ordered directives.

directives.description: Directives that guide the reconstruction process.

reconstruction_fidelity.description:
Target reconstruction fidelity:
- "prototype": Functional demo, fidelity not guaranteed
- "production_equivalent": Functionally equivalent, similar quality
- "bit_identical": Byte-for-byte identical output

SoftwareDefinition.description:
The root object of any S.DEF document.

Contains all layers of software description: system boundary, domain model,
architecture, data models, contracts, behavior, UI, tests, design decisions,
reconstruction rules, dependencies, and deployment requirements.

architecture.description: Architecture — structural layers, modules, and communication patterns.

behavior.description: Behavior — functions, flows, and state machines.

contracts.description: Contracts — interfaces, classes, enums, and API endpoints.

data_models.description: Data model — entities, their attributes, relationships, and validation rules.

domain.description: Domain model — business concepts, rules, and processes.

reconstruction_rules.description: Reconstruction rules — fidelity target, technology constraints, and directives.

resources.description: Resources the software provides or consumes.

system_boundary.description: System boundary — what the software does and does NOT do.

tests.description: Test contracts — unit tests, integration tests, and acceptance criteria.

ui.description: User interface — screens, components, interactions, and navigation.

version.description: Version of the software being described.

description.description: Description of what this interface provides.

type.description: The type of interface (e.g., HTTP, gRPC, CLI, Library).

entity.description: The entity this state machine applies to.

guard_conditions.description: Guard conditions that must be true.

SystemBoundary.description:
Defines the scope of the software — what it does, what it explicitly does NOT do,
who the target users are, and the success criteria.

The `non_goals` field is a critical guardrail: it prevents a reconstruction agent
from over-implementing features that were intentionally excluded.

core_purpose.description: The core purpose of the software in one sentence.

external_dependencies.description: External dependencies at the system level (APIs, services).

non_goals.description: Features explicitly out of scope (prevents over-implementation).

TestContract.description:
The Test Contract is the verification mechanism: it defines the tests
that a reconstructed software implementation must pass to be considered
functionally equivalent to the original.

Tests are described as behavior specifications — given/when/then —
without implementation code.

acceptance_criteria.description: Acceptance criteria for the entire system.

integration_tests.description: Integration tests that span multiple components.

UIBaseElement.description:
Base entity shared by all Pen visual elements.
Every element has a unique `id`, a `type`, and optional position/size.

UIDataBinding.description:
Data binding — links a UI element property to a data entity field.
Enables one-way (display) or two-way (edit) data flow.

UIDesignSystem.description:
A Design System defines the atomic visual primitives — colors, typography,
spacing, shadows, motion, border radius — as named tokens that everything
else references.

Inspired by the Pen format's variable system.

colors.description: Color tokens. Values can be hex colors, or references to other tokens via `$name`.

overrides.description: Token overrides for this theme. Key = token name, value = new value.

UIDocument.description:
A Pen-compatible UI document — a JSON object tree similar to SVG/HTML
but designed for UI design tools and AI consumption.

Compatible with the [Pen format](https://docs.pencil.dev/for-developers/the-pen-format).
All visual elements extend `UIBaseElement`.

S.DEF adds semantic extension fields prefixed with `sdef` to standard Pen
elements — these are ignored by standard Pen parsers but provide essential
context for AI agents (data binding, behaviors, states, accessibility, tests).

UserInterface.description:
The UI section describes the user-facing aspects of the software.

**Three layers of UI description (choose one or combine):**

1. **Design System** (`design_system`) — design tokens, colors, typography,
   spacing, shadows, themes. Higher-level than raw CSS; reusable across screens.
   Adapted from the Pen format's variable system.

2. **Pen-compatible Visual Document** (`document`) — a JSON object tree
   compatible with the [Pen format](https://docs.pencil.dev/for-developers/the-pen-format).
   Uses flexbox layout, fills/strokes/effects, components+instances+slots.
   Best for pixel-level visual fidelity. Extended with S.DEF semantic fields
   (`sdefBindings`, `sdefBehaviors`, `sdefStates`, etc.).

3. **Abstract Screens** (`screens`) — simplified semantic screen descriptions
   without pixel values. Best for intent-level descriptions and quick prototyping.
